mainTopic: The מצוה to finish the cut on יום הכפורים, and the dispute over whether שחיטה counts only at its end or from beginning to end, tested by cases and by the פרה אדומה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about the כהן גדול on יום הכפורים. He cuts the majority of the סימנים, and another כהן completes the cut. The גמרא explains that this finishing causes no invalidation, not even a rabbinic one. It is done only because completing the cut is a מצוה. Next, ריש לקיש (quoting לוי סבא) and רבי יוחנן argue whether שחיטה counts only at its end or from beginning to end. רבא lists cases where everyone agrees: a גוי cutting one סימן, and a bird offering pinched partly below the red line. He then says they argue about one סימן cut outside the עזרה and one inside. רבה בר שימי quotes רב יוסף, who says that case is invalid for everyone, so the dispute is only about a small part cut outside and finished inside. רבי זירא challenges רבי יוחנן from a משנה about the פרה אדומה, and רבא answers that a ruined slaughter was never a slaughter at all. רבא then raises his own difficulty against ריש לקיש about two men slaughtering the פרה. רב יוסף replies that two people may not slaughter one offering, and אביי begins to challenge that answer, continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the cut would be a service done by someone else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that the other כהן's finishing could ever have been thought to make the שחיטה invalid. If his finishing really counted, it would be a יום הכפורים service done by someone other than the כהן גדול, which is not allowed at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it would be a service done by someone else. And a ברייתא teaches that all the services of יום הכפורים are valid only when done by the כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking the suggestion that we 'might have thought' the other כהן's finishing makes the שחיטה invalid. If his part truly mattered, it would plainly be invalid as service by another, not just something we 'might have thought'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier suggestion was that the משנה's rule (a majority is enough) teaches that the other כהן's finishing does not invalidate the שחיטה. The challenge is this: if the finishing were a real part of the שחיטה on a Torah level, the ברייתא would make it clearly invalid. So the 'might have thought' line seems out of place.

keyTerms.meaning: A Temple service done by someone else, not the כהן גדול
The special Temple services of יום הכפורים
Valid only when done by him (the כהן גדול)

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן הָוְיָא לֵיהּ עֲבוֹדָה בְּאַחֵר,
phrases.english: If so, it would be a service performed by another,
phrases.notes: 'If so' means: if the other כהן's finishing really counted as part of the שחיטה.

phrases.english: and it is taught: the entire service of יום הכפורים
is valid only when done by him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן הָוְיָא לֵיהּ עֲבוֹדָה בְּאַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier explanation (from before this section) that the משנה's 'majority' rule teaches about the other כהן finishing the cut on יום הכפורים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that one 'might have thought' the other כהן's finishing would invalidate the שחיטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the finishing mattered on a Torah level, it would definitely be invalid as עבודה באחר, so there is no room for a 'might have thought'.

steps.title: The worry was only a rabbinic invalidation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the 'might have thought' was about a rabbinic invalidation, not a Torah one. The משנה's rule that a majority is enough teaches that there is no invalidation at all, not even a rabbinic one.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: you might have thought it is invalid by rabbinic law, since it could enter your mind that there is a rabbinic invalidation. That is why we learned: 'a majority of one סימן in a bird and a majority of two in an animal.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the worry. It was never a Torah-level problem, only a possible rabbinic one, and the משנה rules that out too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the שחיטה is already complete once the majority is cut, the other כהן's finishing is not a real service at all on a Torah level. One could still have thought the רבנן invalidated it. The משנה's wording, that a majority is enough, shows the רבנן did not.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (the גמרא reinterprets a statement)
Invalid by rabbinic law
It could enter your mind to say (a first assumption we might make)
A majority of one סימן is enough in a bird

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי קָאָמַר: יָכוֹל יְהֵא פָּסוּל מִדְּרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: This is what he is saying: one might think it is invalid by rabbinic law,
for it could enter your mind to say
that there is a rabbinic invalidation,
therefore we learned:
'a majority of one סימן in a bird
and a majority of two סימנים in an animal.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: יָכוֹל יְהֵא פָּסוּל מִדְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1 by changing the worry from a Torah level to a rabbinic level.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the 'might have thought' refers to a rabbinic, not Torah, invalidation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One could have thought the רבנן invalidated a שחיטה finished by another כהן on יום הכפורים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once a majority is cut the שחיטה is complete, and there is no invalidation at all, not even a rabbinic one.

steps.title: Then why finish the cut at all?
steps.stepSummary: If there is not even a rabbinic problem when the majority alone is cut, the גמרא asks why another כהן needs to finish the cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since there is not even a rabbinic invalidation, why do I need to finish the cut?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know a majority is fully enough, the גמרא asks a natural follow-up: what is the point of having the other כהן finish cutting?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling in step 2 seems to make the finishing pointless. The גמרא wants to know what purpose it still serves.

keyTerms.meaning: To finish off or complete (the cutting of the סימנים)
Why do I need it?

phrases.english: And since there is not even a rabbinic invalidation,
why do I need to complete it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמֵאַחַר דַּאֲפִילּוּ פְּסוּלָא דְּרַבָּנַן לֵיכָּא, לְמָה לִי לְמָרֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the answer in step 2, which seems to make the finishing unnecessary.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the purpose of having another כהן finish the cut if the majority already completes the שחיטה?

steps.title: Finishing the cut is a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it is a מצוה to finish cutting the סימנים, even though the שחיטה is already valid without it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a מצוה to finish the cut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short answer: finishing is not needed for the animal to be valid, but it is still a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This separates two levels: what is needed for validity (a majority) and what is the proper way to do it (finishing the cut). The other כהן finishes the cut because doing it fully is a מצוה, not because the שחיטה would be invalid without it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a מצוה (the proper way) to finish the cut

steps.whatToRemember: On יום הכפורים the כהן גדול cuts the majority, and that alone makes the שחיטה valid, with no Torah or rabbinic problem. Another כהן finishes the cut only because it is a מצוה to do so.

phrases.english: It is a מצוה to complete it.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Completing the cut is a מצוה, even though validity is achieved with the majority.

steps.title: When does שחיטה take effect: only at the end, or the whole way through?
steps.stepSummary: A new topic begins. ריש לקיש, quoting לוי סבא, says שחיטה counts only at its end. רבי יוחנן says שחיטה counts from the beginning all the way to the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said in the name of לוי סבא: שחיטה happens only at the end. And רבי יוחנן said: שחיטה happens from the beginning until the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion with a dispute between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן about the point at which the act of שחיטה actually counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, only the final moment (when the needed amount is completed) is the real שחיטה. For רבי יוחנן, every part of the cutting, from the first stroke, is part of the שחיטה. In the next steps רבא first gives cases where both sides agree, and then names the case where they really disagree (step 8).

keyTerms.meaning: שחיטה counts only at its end
שחיטה counts from the beginning to the end

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש does not mean that the beginning of the cut is unnecessary. He means the legal 'moment of שחיטה' is only when it is completed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute decides how we judge cases where the cut is split between people or interrupted, which the גמרא goes on to explore.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם לֵוִי סָבָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said in the name of Levi the Elder:
slaughter is only at the end,
and Rabbi Yochanan said:
slaughter is from the beginning until the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם לֵוִי סָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from the יום הכפורים discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש (in the name of לוי סבא): שחיטה takes effect only at its end. רבי יוחנן: שחיטה takes effect throughout, from start to finish.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: a גוי cut one סימן, a Jew cut the other
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts setting the limits of the dispute. Everyone agrees that if a גוי cut one סימן and a Jew cut the other, the animal is invalid. The גוי's cut is an act that makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Everyone agrees that where a גוי cut one סימן and a Jew cut one סימן, it is invalid, because an act that makes it a טרפה was done to it by a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins defining where ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן do not argue. He starts with a case where both agree the animal is invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even ריש לקיש, who says only the end counts, agrees here. The גוי's cut is not a valid שחיטה, so it simply damages the animal and makes it a טרפה before the Jew finishes. The problem is not about when שחיטה takes effect; the animal was already ruined by an invalid cut.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
One of the two organs cut in שחיטה (windpipe or food pipe)
An act that makes the animal a טרפה (fatally damaged and forbidden)
By the hand of a non-Jew

phrases.english: Rava said: everyone agrees,
phrases.notes: 'Everyone' means both ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן from the last step.

phrases.english: where a gentile cut one siman,
and a Jew cut one siman,
that it is invalid,
since an act of making it a tereifa was done to it
by the hand of a gentile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts marking out the limits of the dispute in step 5 by giving a case where both sides agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a גוי cut one סימן and a Jew cut the other, the animal is invalid according to everyone, because the גוי's invalid cut made it a טרפה.

steps.title: Another case everyone agrees on: the bird burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds a second case where everyone agrees the offering is invalid. This is an עולת העוף where one סימן was pinched below the red line and one above it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Likewise with a bird burnt offering: if the כהן pinched one סימן below the line and one סימן above it, it is invalid. By pinching below, he did an act that belongs to a bird sin offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues his list of cases where both ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן agree. Here the case is a bird burnt offering pinched partly below and partly above the red line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולת העוף belongs above the red line on the מזבח, and a חטאת העוף belongs below it. Pinching one סימן below already counts as doing a חטאת העוף act on the bird. So the bird is ruined as a burnt offering no matter how we view the timing of שחיטה. Just like the גוי case in step 6, the first act ruins it, so the dispute never comes up.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird burnt offering, done above the red line on the מזבח
A bird sin offering, done below the red line
Pinching: how a כהן kills a bird offering, cutting the neck with his fingernail
Below / above the red line that divides the מזבח in half

phrases.english: In a bird burnt offering as well,
where he pinched one siman below
phrases.notes: Below and above mean below or above the red line around the middle of the מזבח.

phrases.english: and one siman above, it is invalid,
because he did with it
an act of a bird sin offering below.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second agreed-upon case to רבא's list from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עולת העוף pinched one סימן below the line and one above is invalid according to everyone, because a חטאת העוף act was done to it.

steps.title: רבא's case of dispute: one סימן outside, one inside
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the dispute applies only where one סימן was cut outside the עזרה and the other inside. רבי יוחנן's view makes the person liable, and ריש לקיש's view does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree only where he cut one סימן outside and one סימן inside. Whoever says שחיטה counts from beginning to end holds he is liable. Whoever says שחיטה counts only at the end holds he is not liable.
steps.whatsHappening: After listing the cases where everyone agrees, רבא now names the one case where ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן really disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting a קרבן outside the עזרה brings a punishment. According to רבי יוחנן, the beginning of the cut already counts as שחיטה, so the outside part makes him liable. According to ריש לקיש, only the end counts, and the end happened inside, so he is not liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside / inside the עזרה (the בית המקדש courtyard)
"They disagree only in…": narrows a dispute down to one case
He is liable to punishment

steps.whyThisMatters: This is רבא's practical test case for the dispute from step 5. The very next step will challenge it.

phrases.english: They disagree only
in a case where he cut one siman outside
phrases.notes: Outside and inside mean outside or inside the עזרה, the courtyard where קרבנות must be slaughtered.

phrases.english: and one siman inside.
According to the one who says slaughter counts
from the beginning to the end, he is liable.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵינָהּ לִשְׁחִיטָה אֶלָּא בַּסּוֹף –
phrases.english: According to the one who says slaughter counts only at the end,
he is not liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא כְּגוֹן שֶׁשָּׁחַט סִימָן אֶחָד בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the agreed cases to the one case of dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבא's view, the dispute applies when one סימן is cut outside and one inside. רבי יוחנן holds he is liable, and ריש לקיש holds he is not.

steps.title: רבה בר שימי: our teacher said that case is invalid for everyone
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שימי objects to רבא's case of dispute. He quotes רב יוסף, who said that cutting one סימן outside and one inside is invalid according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שימי said to רבא: "Our Master did not say it this way." Who is the Master? רב יוסף. He said that where one סימן was cut outside and one inside, it is also invalid, because he did an act of a bird sin offering outside.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר שימי challenges רבא's case by quoting their teacher רב יוסף. רב יוסף put the one-outside-one-inside case on the "everyone agrees" list, not the dispute list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's reasoning matches the bird case in step 7. Cutting one סימן outside is already a complete act, like a חטאת העוף, done outside. So it counts as an outside slaughter for everyone, whatever view one holds on timing. This means רבא's case cannot be where the two sides disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Master": a respectful way to refer to one's teacher
"And who is he?": asking who is meant
"Did not say it this way": pointing out a different version of a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: רבה בר שימי is not arguing about the הלכה of ריש לקיש or רבי יוחנן. He is arguing about which case their dispute applies to.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Shimi said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבא, who gave the cases in steps 6 through 8.

phrases.english: The Master did not say it this way.
And who is he? Rav Yosef.
Where he cut one siman outside
and one siman inside, it is also invalid,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי עָשָׂה בָּהּ מַעֲשֵׂה חַטַּאת הָעוֹף בַּחוּץ.
phrases.english: because he did with it an act of a bird sin offering outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's case of dispute from step 8 by citing a different tradition from רב יוסף.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the dispute is about one סימן outside and one inside.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cutting one full סימן outside is already a complete act done outside, so everyone agrees the slaughter is invalid. The case cannot be where the dispute applies.

steps.title: רב יוסף's case of dispute: a small part cut outside, finished inside
steps.stepSummary: In רב יוסף's version, the dispute applies only where a small part of the סימנים was cut outside and the cut was finished inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree only where he cut a minority of the סימנים outside and finished inside. Whoever says שחיטה counts from beginning to end holds he is liable. Whoever says it counts only at the end holds he is not liable.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing רב יוסף's teaching, the גמרא gives his version of the one case where ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן really disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting only a small part (מיעוט) outside is not a complete act of any kind, so there is no automatic invalidation. The case depends entirely on the dispute. רבי יוחנן says the start counts, so he is liable. ריש לקיש says only the end counts, and the end was inside, so he is not liable.

keyTerms.meaning: A minority (small part) of the סימנים
He finished it, meaning he completed the cut

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: the dispute is about one סימן outside and one inside. רב יוסף (quoted by רבה בר שימי): that case is invalid for everyone. The dispute is only about a small part cut outside and finished inside.

phrases.english: They disagree only
in a case where he cut a minority of the simanim outside
and finished it inside.
According to the one who says slaughter counts
from the beginning to the end, he is liable.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵינָהּ לִשְׁחִיטָה אֶלָּא בַּסּוֹף –
phrases.english: According to the one who says slaughter counts only at the end,
he is not liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא כְּגוֹן שֶׁשָּׁחַט מִיעוּט סִימָנִין בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב יוסף's teaching by giving his replacement case of dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב יוסף, the dispute applies only when a minority of the סימנים is cut outside and the cut is finished inside. רבי יוחנן holds he is liable, and ריש לקיש holds he is not.

steps.title: רבי זירא quotes a משנה about the red heifer
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא quotes a משנה from מסכת פרה. During the slaughter, a problem stops all clothes from becoming impure. During the sprinkling, only people who worked on it after the problem are spared.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objects from a משנה. Everyone who works on the פרה from start to finish makes his clothes impure, and doing other work while busy with it disqualifies the פרה. If a problem happened during its slaughter, the clothes do not become impure, whether the person worked on it before or after the problem. If the problem happened during the sprinkling, people who worked on it before the problem get impure clothes, and people who worked on it after do not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא is setting up a challenge by quoting a משנה about the פרה אדומה. The actual question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is the different outcomes. A problem during the שחיטה cancels impurity for everyone, even those who worked before the problem. A problem during the הזאה cancels it only for those who came after the problem. רבי זירא will use this difference against the view that שחיטה exists from beginning to end.

keyTerms.meaning: The red heifer, whose ashes are used to purify people from impurity caused by a dead body
Make clothes impure. The people who work on the פרה become impure, and so do the clothes they wear
Other, unrelated work done while busy with the פרה, which disqualifies it
A disqualification, something that makes the offering invalid
Sprinkling the פרה's blood

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira raises an objection:
All those who are busy with the heifer
phrases.notes: This is the פרה אדומה. The quote comes from משנה פרה 4:4.

phrases.english: from the beginning until the end
make garments impure,
and they disqualify it by doing other work.
If a disqualification happened to it during its slaughter,
whether before its disqualification
or after its disqualification,
it does not make garments impure;
if it happened during its sprinkling:
phrases.notes: This means the sprinkling of the פרה's blood, the step that comes after the slaughter.

phrases.english: before its disqualification, it makes garments impure,
after its disqualification, it does not make garments impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside source, a משנה, to test the dispute about when שחיטה takes effect.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that שחיטה exists from the beginning to the end of the cut.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step only quotes the source. The argument built on it comes in step 12.

steps.title: The משנה should split the slaughter case too
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא argues that if שחיטה happens throughout the whole cut, the משנה should make the same before-and-after split for slaughter that it makes for sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose you say that slaughter exists from the beginning to the end. Then the משנה should also make a split in the slaughter. If a problem happened during the slaughter, people who worked on it before the problem would get impure clothes, and people who worked on it after would not!
steps.whatsHappening: Here רבי זירא makes his actual challenge. He says the משנה does not fit the view that שחיטה exists from beginning to end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the slaughter counts from the very first moment of the cut. Then the part done before the problem was a real, valid slaughter, just like sprinkling done before a problem. So those people should get impure clothes. The משנה says no one does, which suggests slaughter counts only at the end.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it make a distinction. The source should have split the case into two outcomes

phrases.english: And if you say
that slaughter exists from the beginning until the end,
let it also make a distinction in its slaughter:
if a disqualification happened to it during slaughter,
before its disqualification, it makes garments impure,
after its disqualification, it does not make garments impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ יֶשְׁנָהּ לִשְׁחִיטָה מִתְּחִלָּה וְעַד סוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה quoted in step 11 to attack the beginning-to-end view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that שחיטה exists from the beginning to the end of the cut.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the first part of the cut is already real slaughter, then the work done before a problem should count, just as it does with sprinkling. The משנה treats slaughter differently, so slaughter must count only at the end.

steps.title: A ruined slaughter was never a slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that when a שחיטה is ruined, it becomes clear looking back that it was never a slaughter at all. So nothing done during it counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Are you talking about a slaughter that got ruined? There it is different, because it becomes clear, looking back, that it was not a slaughter at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends the beginning-to-end view. He explains why the משנה does not split the slaughter case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sprinkling is made of separate acts, so the sprinkles done before a problem stay valid. A slaughter is one act, and if it ends up ruined, the whole act is shown never to have been a slaughter. So even the part before the problem never counted, and this fits the beginning-to-end view.

keyTerms.meaning: It became ruined or spoiled
There it is different. This phrase marks a case as an exception
The matter was revealed retroactively: later events show what was true from the start

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא's challenge does not disprove that שחיטה exists from beginning to end. A slaughter that ends up ruined was never a slaughter in the first place, so nobody who worked on it gets impure clothes.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Are you talking about a slaughter that was ruined?
There it is different,
because the matter was revealed looking back
that it is not a slaughter at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge from step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the case: a ruined slaughter is treated as never having been a slaughter.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The part of the cut done before the problem was a real slaughter, so the משנה should have split the slaughter case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once the slaughter is ruined, it is revealed looking back that there was never any slaughter. So no part of it makes clothes impure, and the beginning-to-end view still stands.

steps.title: רבא's own difficulty: the משנה should mention two slaughterers
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that, according to the view that שחיטה happens only at the end, the משנה should have taught a case where two men slaughter a valid פרה. The first man would not become impure, but the second would.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If anything bothers me, this is what bothers me. Take the one who says a slaughter only counts at its end. The משנה should have made a split even with a valid פרה. For example, if two men slaughtered it, the first man would not become impure, and the second man would become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a new question of his own. This time it is against the view that a שחיטה only happens at the very end of the cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whoever slaughters the פרה אדומה becomes impure. If the slaughter only 'happens' at the final moment, then a man who started the cut and handed it off never really slaughtered, so he should stay pure. The man who finished it should become impure. Since the משנה never teaches this split, it seems to argue against that view.

keyTerms.term: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי
keyTerms.meaning: If anything is hard for me, this is what is hard for me
A valid (not ruined) פרה אדומה
Makes a person impure

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי,
phrases.english: If anything is difficult for me, this is what is difficult for me:

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵינָהּ לִשְׁחִיטָה אֶלָּא בַּסּוֹף,
phrases.english: according to the one who says slaughter only counts at the end,
let the משנה make a split even with a valid פרה,
for example, where two men slaughtered it,
where it does not make the first man impure,
and it does make the last man impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the 'throughout' view in step 13, רבא turns to a difficulty against the other view, that slaughter counts only at the end.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that שחיטה happens only at the end of the cut.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only the final moment counts, a man who did the first part of the cut never slaughtered and should stay pure, while the one who finished should become impure. The משנה should have taught this split, but it doesn't.

steps.title: Two men may not slaughter one offering
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the case of two slaughterers can't be taught, because a ברייתא learns from a פסוק that two people may not slaughter one offering together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: You are talking about two men slaughtering one offering? Ask anything except that! We learned: 'תזבח' teaches that two people may not slaughter one offering. 'תזבחהו' teaches that one person may not slaughter two offerings at once.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף knocks out רבא's question by saying the case it depends on is not allowed in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's question needed two men to slaughter the same פרה. רב יוסף points to a ברייתא that forbids two people from slaughtering one offering. So the משנה had no reason to teach a case that should never happen.

keyTerms.meaning: Except for that one; ask anything but this
An offering
You shall slaughter/offer
You shall slaughter it

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Are you saying two men on one offering?
Leave that one out,
for we learned: 'You shall slaughter',

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ שְׁנַיִם שׁוֹחֲטִין זֶבַח אֶחָד,
phrases.english: that two may not slaughter one offering;
'You shall slaughter it',

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא אֶחָד שׁוֹחֵט שְׁנֵי זְבָחִים.
phrases.english: that one may not slaughter two offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's difficulty in step 14 by rejecting the case it depends on.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the premise: the case of two slaughterers is not allowed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה could have taught a valid פרה slaughtered by two men.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two people may not slaughter one offering, so the משנה would not teach such a case.

steps.title: How the spelling of the word teaches 'one slaughterer'
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא explains that the word is written in a way that reads as singular, 'תזבחהו', which shows that only one person should slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב כהנא said: It is written 'תזבחהו' (singular).
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא explains how the ברייתא got its rule from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is read in the plural ('you all shall slaughter it'), which could suggest that many people may slaughter together. But it is spelled without a ו, so it can be read in the singular, 'you (one person) shall slaughter it'. The singular spelling is the source for 'not two people on one offering.'

keyTerms.meaning: It is written (how the word is spelled)
'You (singular) shall slaughter it', the reading based on the spelling

phrases.english: And Rav Kahana said:
'You shall slaughter it' (singular) is written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the derivation in the ברייתא quoted in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The singular spelling of the word in the פסוק teaches that one person, not two, slaughters an offering.

steps.title: אביי: isn't that only one תנא's opinion?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף. In the name of רבי יוחנן, it was said that this ברייתא is only the view of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Wasn't it said about this that רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This is the opinion of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins to push back on רב יוסף's answer. His statement continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ban on two slaughterers is only the view of one תנא, then the other רבנן may allow it. In that case רבא's question could come back for them. אביי is weakening the answer from step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it so? (a word that opens a challenge)
It was said about it (a later comment on this source)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Wasn't it said about it,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: This is the opinion of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's answer in step 15 by narrowing its source to one תנא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that two people may never slaughter one offering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא is only the view of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, others may allow two slaughterers. Then the case רבא asked about is possible.
